title: Apple researchers identify trade-offs in large language model conditioning
excerpt: A study finds efficient steering methods often reduce fluency and that instruction-tuned models show lower effectiveness for activation steering.
bodyHtml:
Apple researchers published a systematic study on September 30, 2026, investigating the effectiveness and fluency trade-offs in conditioning large language models. The study examined various methods for injecting or removing target concepts from model outputs, noting that current approaches often focus on effectiveness while neglecting generation quality.

The findings indicate that efficient steering methods frequently achieve conditioning at a steep cost to fluency. Additionally, the researchers identified that activation steering methods, which guide generative model behavior, are far less effective on instruction-tuned models than on their base counterparts. The study also found that simple prompting and supervised fine-tuning are viable options for concept injection, but are not as good at concept removal.

The researchers observed that cheaply computed textual metrics highly correlate to costly LLM-as-judge scores. These metrics provide insights into the behavior of conditioning methods.
topic: On the Effectiveness-Fluency Trade-Off in LLM Conditioning: A Systematic Study
